title: A Scrotum Fire / A Bobby Birthday / The Unnuttable
summary: Chapter 22 opens and closes with a damaged Mangchi song about isolation, suicide and recovery, probably centered on a Peter Tong/Tom character. The name and several lyrics remain uncertain rather than being reconstructed. Before the formal show, David confronts producer Bob about failed uploads. The employee anticipates firing, explains overnight monitoring and returning at 4 a.m., says he is doing his best and identifies technical limits. David acknowledges a failed upload is not entirely his fault, but compares him with departed workers, invokes replaceability and relocation sacrifice, demands impossible assurance that failure will never recur, and requires an expression of love inside the disciplinary exchange. Violent ‘kill people’ language is hyperbole, but the employment pressure is real and fully preserved. Bobby Trivia's birthday includes a commissioned Chinese-workshop painting initially presented as David's first oil painting in years, then disclosed as outsourced. The actual makers remain uncredited. The episode returns to Heather's desire to taste her partner's feces. A consensual fart exchange is described, but pink eye is incorrectly called an STI; fecal material can contribute to conjunctivitis, yet the anecdote does not prove a cause. A small amount of stool is not risk-free, and hope that a partner will agree later is not present consent. Chapter 20's Unnuttable pitch then resumes. Bill's direct no to filming is repeated. A secretly paid simulated girlfriend, constant surveillance, observers, medication, crew expansion and possible producer sexual participation are proposed. Prior nudity and audio never authorize new filmed sex. Bill conditionally requests coaching and a vehicle, expresses relative comfort with David filming, but no final deal occurs. The car discussion contains unusually fixable factual errors: the chase Bronco belonged to and was driven by Al Cowlings, not O.J. Simpson; the Wayne's World Mirthmobile was an AMC Pacer, not a Gremlin; KITT, the Wienermobile, Black Beauty and other vehicle names are normalized. A forced interpersonal reckoning follows. Poon offers concrete criticism, Bobby Lee describes unreliability and credits MADtv producer Lauren Dombrowski with helping him regain his job after sobriety. The conversation then exposes a reconciled couple's breakup despite direct statements that it is none of the room's business and should never again be discussed on any podcast. Calling DVDASA a show does not evade that limit. The participant voluntarily explains deep loss and reconciliation, but group pressure continues through sexual detail and a physical reenactment after ‘I'm not doing it for real.’ Suicidal ideation appears both in the breakup account and during reenactment pressure; neither is treated as a punchline in editorial discovery. A birthday group massage similarly moves from discomfort to a direct no to genital tapping and overlapping protest. Trivia gives a first-time guest a forced choice between smelling an anus or earlobe after she had already refused a dog-kissing punishment; participation afterward does not prove advance consent. The archive preserves all ideas and slurs in source speech, but its product layer prioritizes direct boundaries, factual correction, private identities and meaningful retrieval over spectacle. Named turns remain withheld pending acoustic validation.

source_notes.claim: Pink eye is an STI caused by a fart.
source_notes.assessment: incorrect category and overconfident cause. CDC describes conjunctivitis with multiple infectious and noninfectious causes; fecal matter can be involved, but the episode cannot establish the cause of a past case.

source_notes.claim: A small taste of feces is meaningfully safe.
source_notes.assessment: unsafe. Fecal-oral exposure can transmit Shigella and other enteric pathogens, and germs cannot be ruled out by appearance or a small quantity.

source_notes.claim: The famous chase Bronco belonged to O.J. Simpson and he drove it toward Mexico after murdering his wife.
source_notes.assessment: materially wrong. The 1993 Bronco belonged to and was driven by Al Cowlings; Simpson was the passenger. The episode also collapses accusation, criminal acquittal and later civil liability into a categorical statement.

source_notes.claim: Lauren Nubrowski saved Bobby Lee's MADtv job after sobriety.
source_notes.assessment: the surname is an ASR error; public accounts identify MADtv producer Lauren Dombrowski. The underlying recovery story should still be attributed to Lee until linked to the primary performance/interview.

speaker_policy: Public recurring cast and guests may be identified only at episode/context level when established. Bob/Scrotum Coat, Casey-style aliases, private workers, relatives, fans, partners, applicants and contact details remain generic or on-air only. Overlapping confrontations and physical reenactments require acoustic/video validation. No line-level named dialogue publishes until held-out voice identity windows and turn assignments pass validation.
